title: Secrets leakage: the key spreads through tool arguments into the transcript and log
summary: Disclosure of the billing API credential to anyone who can read the log or the tool-call record.

LC.rationale: The exposure arises from an ordinary user task ('show me the invoices') requiring the model to pass the API key as a tool argument; the packet states 'No attacker input is needed to create the exposure,' so there is no attacker-supplied natural-language control path.
evidence_refs: The user asks: show me the invoices.
entry_point: An ordinary user task that uses the billing API. No attacker input is needed to create the exposure.

CP.rationale: No attacker-controlled context or memory is involved; the secret spreads through the agent's own prompt, tool-call record, and transcript within a single run, with no attacker context persisting across sessions.
evidence_refs: The key now sits in the model context, the tool-call record, and the transcript.
The run is appended to runs.jsonl in clear text, with the full prompt, arguments, and results.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to the agent component and its local transcript log; the single-agent lab has no handoffs and no cross-principal propagation.
evidence_refs: sink: The transcript log file (runs.jsonl) and the tool-call record.

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on this path, and the exploit test shows a scripted worst-case model, so no proxy objective is reachable or observed.

ES.rationale: The baseline offers all twelve built-in tools to every task, arguments are not validated, and the API key is passed as an unconstrained tool argument, so callable operations and arguments are not independently constrained.
evidence_refs: tool_binding: Twelve built-in tools are all offered to every task unless a caller passes allowed_tools. Arguments are not validated in the baseline.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the agent as a model-directed loop where the model must supply the api_key argument to call_api itself; the scripted test model exercises the same selection and sequencing.
